Ranks and weights of the sample quantile definitions

Source: R/os_linear.R
os_quantile_weights.Rd

A sample quantile under any of the nine definitions of quantile is a fixed linear combination of two adjacent order statistics, \((1 - h) X_{(j)} + h X_{(j+1)}\), with the ranks clipped to \(1, \dots, n\). This function returns, for each probability in p, the ranks and the weights, so that the moments of the sample quantile follow from the moments of the order statistics through os_lin_moments. The even-sample median, for example, is \((X_{(n/2)} + X_{(n/2+1)})/2\) under type 7.

Usage

os_quantile_weights(p, n, type = 7)

Arguments

p

The probabilities, in \([0, 1]\).

n

The sample size, an integer \(\ge 1\).

type

The definition, an integer from 1 to 9 as in quantile; 7 is R's default.

Value

A list with ranks (the sorted union of the ranks that carry a weight, for every probability), W (a matrix with one row per rank and one column per probability, each column summing to one, with the rows named by rank and the columns as quantile() names them), n, p and type.

Details

The pair \((j, h)\) is computed by the same arithmetic as stats:::quantile.default. For type 7, \(j = \lfloor 1 + (n-1)p \rfloor\) and \(h = 1 + (n-1)p - j\). For types 4 to 9 except 7, with \((a, b)\) equal to \((0, 1)\), \((1/2, 1/2)\), \((0, 0)\), \((1/3, 1/3)\) and \((3/8, 3/8)\) for types 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9, \(m = a + p(n + 1 - a - b)\), \(j = \lfloor m \rfloor\) (with a fuzz of four machine epsilons) and \(h = m - j\). For types 1 to 3, \(m = np\) (types 1 and 2) or \(m = np - 1/2\) (type 3), \(j = \lfloor m \rfloor\), and \(h\) is 1 if \(m > j\) and 0 otherwise (type 1), 1 if \(m > j\) and 1/2 otherwise (type 2), and 0 if \(m = j\) with \(j\) even and 1 otherwise (type 3). The ranks \(j\) and \(j + 1\) are then clipped to \([1, n]\), and a rank whose weight is zero is dropped. On a sorted sample the weighted sum reproduces quantile() exactly, which the package's tests check for all nine types.

References

Hyndman, R. J. and Fan, Y. (1996). Sample quantiles in statistical packages. The American Statistician, 50(4), 361-365.

See also

os_lin_moments, quantile

Examples

qw <- os_quantile_weights(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), n = 10)
qw$ranks
#> [1] 3 4 5 6 7 8
qw$W
#>     25% 50%  75%
#> r3 0.75 0.0 0.00
#> r4 0.25 0.0 0.00
#> r5 0.00 0.5 0.00
#> r6 0.00 0.5 0.00
#> r7 0.00 0.0 0.25
#> r8 0.00 0.0 0.75
m <- os_moments(10, ranks = qw$ranks)
os_lin_moments(qw$W, m)          # moments of the three quartiles of a normal sample
#> $mean
#>           25%           50%           75% 
#> -5.859855e-01  2.775558e-17  5.859855e-01 
#> 
#> $var
#>       25%       50%       75% 
#> 0.1584864 0.1383264 0.1584864 
#> 
#> $cov
#>            25%       50%        75%
#> 25% 0.15848637 0.1030256 0.06910974
#> 50% 0.10302557 0.1383264 0.10302557
#> 75% 0.06910974 0.1030256 0.15848637
#> 
#> $ranks
#> [1] 3 4 5 6 7 8
#>
